answer: A desert economy stays honest when each new identity must lead a distinct caravan that must wander from oasis to oasis, steering by a different nebula while a distinct guide stamps each water skin. The first fake owes one skin, the second eight, the third twenty-seven, since the nth fake owes the cube of its number, so the tenth fake alone owes a thousand skins and twenty fakes owe 44,100. Bulk farming fails because one porter carries one skin per crossing, each skin is sealed to one route, and one guide walks one caravan at a time, like one shepherd leading one flock across the sand.
